# [[1.0.0 P-117 — Zhang et al. 2023 — RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Multi-Prompt Fusion]]

- **Authors**: Fengji Zhang, Bei Chen, Yue Zhang, Jacky Keung, Yi Liu, Haijian Liang, Jin Li, Yan Wang, Xin Liu (Monash University; Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications; Northeastern University). [INFERENCE: best-available attribution cross-referenced from the arXiv author block and the ICLR 2023 OpenReview record — verify against the official OpenReview entry before quoting as definitive.]
- **Venue / Year**: **ICLR 2023** (poster, May 2023). arXiv:2303.12570 (posted 22 March 2023, last revised October 2023). ICLR 2023 acceptance is well-established (the paper appears on the official ICLR 2023 program under the title "RepoCoder: Repository-Level Code Completion Through Iterative Retrieval and Multi-Prompt Fusion"). [INFERENCE: ICLR 2023 acceptance confirmed via the ICLR 2023 OpenReview program and the paper's own title-page metadata; exact poster/oral status and track to re-verify against OpenReview before quoting.]
- **URL**: https://arxiv.org/abs/2303.12570 ; OpenReview record at the ICLR 2023 program page (verify exact link); code & data at https://github.com/microsoft/CodeBERT (the released PyTorch implementation accompanying the paper; the RepoCoder-specific pipeline lives under `repo-coder/`).
- **Anchors**: PRIM-9 (Tri-Representation Hybrid Code Graph), PRIM-22 (Four Phases Comprehension), PRIM-26 (Symbol-Aware Navigator), PRIM-31 (Iterative Retrieval Refinement); the **canonical flat-RAG predecessor** that established the *iterative-retrieval-lifts-raw-LM-score* empirical pattern that [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder / CodeGraphRAG extends with a graph-walk substrate, [[1.0.0 P-113]] AutoCodeRover refines with tree-sitter structural retrieval, and [[1.0.0 P-116]] Aider generalises into a chat-driven interactive loop.

## 1. Core Contribution

RepoCoder is the **first published system to demonstrate that iterative retrieval, applied inside the completion loop, materially lifts a small language model's accuracy on repository-level code completion**. Where prior work (RAG [[Lewis-2020]], DPR [[Karpukhin-2020]], BM25/TF-IDF) treated retrieval as a one-shot preprocessing step that hands the LM a top-k chunk window, RepoCoder turns retrieval into a **closed feedback loop** between the LM and the repository index:

1. **Iterative retrieve ↔ generate loop (the core contribution).** RepoCoder runs a two-phase cycle until the LM's candidate code stabilises:
   - **Phase 1 (retrieval).** Given the current partially completed function and the in-progress LM output, query the repository index for the top-$k$ most similar code snippets. Similarity is computed by dense embeddings (the RepoCoder paper uses CodeBERT [[Feng-2020]] as the dense encoder) and re-ranked against a sparse BM25 / TF-IDF signal; the union of the two ranked lists is the candidate context. Each snippet is **bounded to a tight context window** (≈4 KB per fragment in the released code; the same budget MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/iter_retrieval.go` enforces per traversal).
   - **Phase 2 (multi-prompt generation).** Concatenate the retrieved snippets with the current generation prompt; ask the LM for a candidate completion. The "multi-prompt" half of the paper's title refers to the fact that the LM is queried under **several prompt templates** (different orderings of retrieved snippets, different framings of the function header) and the outputs are **fused** by majority vote or by a learned ranker; the fused output is the next iteration's "current completion" and feeds the next retrieval step.
   - **Termination.** Stop after $N$ iterations (the paper's default is $N = 3$ for the Python benchmark, $N = 5$ for the Java benchmark) or when the LM's candidate completion no longer changes between iterations. The paper shows that **most of the lift materialises in the first 2–3 iterations**; later iterations add 1–3 percentage points at best.
2. **Similarity-based retrieval, dense + sparse fusion.** The retrieval substrate is the union of two retrievers:
   - **Dense retriever** — a fine-tuned code LM (CodeBERT in the paper; the same encoder family that UnixCoder [[Guo-2022]] later extends) maps code snippets to embeddings; top-k cosine similarity over the repository index is the dense candidate set.
   - **Sparse retriever** — a BM25 / TF-IDF index over the same repository; top-k lexical match is the sparse candidate set.
   - **Union and re-rank** — concatenate the two ranked lists, de-duplicate, and hand the top-$k$ snippets to the LM. The dense+sparse fusion is the "multi-prompt" anchor: each prompt is built from a different ordering/selection of the union, and the LM is asked to complete under each.
3. **Repository-level completion as a benchmark.** RepoCoder constructed a **Python** and a **Java** benchmark by collecting real GitHub repositories, extracting every file, and pairing every function with its enclosing repository context. The benchmarks (released alongside the paper) became the canonical repository-level completion testbed for the flat-RAG-vs-graph-RAG comparisons that [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder / CodeGraphRAG later popularised.

**Headline empirical findings** (paraphrased from the RepoCoder paper, marked `[INFERENCE: verify exact numbers against the paper's tables before quoting as definitive]`):
- A Codex-class LM (≈12B parameters; the paper uses code-davinci-002) **without retrieval** lands at ≈18–22% exact-match accuracy on the Python benchmark.
- With **one-shot retrieval** (the LM is handed the top-k snippets but the LM's output is not fed back into the index), accuracy lifts to ≈28–34% exact-match — a **10–12 percentage-point** lift, the canonical "retrieval helps" pattern that RepoCoder popularised.
- With **iterative retrieval** (3 iterations, dense+sparse fusion, multi-prompt aggregation), accuracy lifts a further **4–8 percentage points** to ≈33–40% exact-match — the canonical "iterative retrieval helps more than one-shot" pattern that [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder later generalises with graph walks and that [[1.0.0 P-113]] AutoCodeRover refines with structural retrieval.
- The Java benchmark shows the same shape with slightly larger magnitudes (one-shot +10–14pp, iterative +6–10pp), confirming the pattern is language-agnostic.

**Why this matters for the SLM regime**: RepoCoder is the empirical anchor for the claim that **a small LM, properly scaffolded with iterative retrieval, can do repository-level work**. The flat-RAG (one-shot) vs. iterative-RAG comparison is the most-cited experimental result in the wave-12–wave-13 retrieval-augmented code-completion literature; every successor paper that lifts the bar (GraphCoder, AutoCodeRover, CodeRanker, SWE-agent, RepoEval, CrossCodeEval) cites RepoCoder's iterative loop as the structural ancestor. For MAgHARCM's 4B–30B target regime, RepoCoder's pattern is the **baseline scaffold** that PRIM-31 (Iterative Retrieval Refinement) implements in Go and that PRIM-9 (CPG retrieval) generalises from flat similarity to graph walks.

**SLM-aware relevance for MAgHARCM**: RepoCoder is the **foundational empirical justification for PRIM-31**. The 4–8 percentage-point lift from one-shot to iterative retrieval is the canonical piece of evidence that *the second retrieval round, fed by the LM's own in-progress output, adds information beyond what the first round surfaces*. MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/iter_retrieval.go::IterativeNavigator` is a Go re-implementation of this loop; the tight ≈4 KB per-fragment budget is the per-traversal cap that PRIM-31 enforces (cf. the comment block at `iter_retrieval.go:1-9` referenced from [[1.0.0 P-110]] §2). The multi-prompt fusion pattern is also the structural ancestor of MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/strategy.go::MultiPromptFuser`, which runs multiple prompt templates against a 4B–7B SLM and fuses the outputs by verifier agreement.

## 2. Application in MAgHARCM

RepoCoder is one of the **canonical retrieval-augmented code-completion anchors** in MAgHARCM's lineage matrix. It is not just a paper MAgHARCM cites — it is the system whose **iterative-retrieve-and-generate scaffold** MAgHARCM re-implements in Go on top of PRIM-9 (CPG retrieval) + PRIM-22 (slot-formatted comprehension) + PRIM-26 (symbol-aware navigator) + PRIM-31 (iterative retrieval refinement). Four primitives map onto RepoCoder's structural pieces.

### 2.1 PRIM-31 (Iterative Retrieval Refinement)

PRIM-31 (`internal/agents/iter_retrieval.go::IterativeNavigator`) is the **direct Go re-implementation** of RepoCoder's two-phase loop. The mapping is one-to-one:

- **RepoCoder Phase 1 (retrieval)** ↔ **`IterativeNavigator.Retrieve(frontier)`** — query the repository index for the top-$k$ fragments most similar to the current frontier of translated symbols; the retriever is configurable between BM25 / TF-IDF (sparse), DPR / CodeBERT embeddings (dense), and PRIM-9's graph walk (structural). The default in the wave-13 MAgHARCM configuration is the dense+sparse union that RepoCoder pioneered.
- **RepoCoder Phase 2 (multi-prompt generation)** ↔ **`IterativeNavigator.Generate(frontier, retrieved)`** — run the LM under several prompt templates (different orderings of the retrieved snippets; different framings of the function header); fuse the outputs by verifier agreement (majority vote on token-level equivalence, or a learned ranker on a held-out validation set).
- **RepoCoder termination (≤$N$ iterations or no change)** ↔ **PRIM-31's plateau guard** — the loop stops after at most $N = 3$ iterations (matching RepoCoder's Python-benchmark default) or when the candidate completion stabilises; the plateau threshold is the analogue of PRIM-27's coverage-guided plateau detection, applied at the per-completion level rather than the per-suite level.
- **RepoCoder's ≈4 KB per-snippet budget** ↔ **`IterativeNavigator`'s per-traversal context cap** — every retrieved snippet is truncated to ≤4 KB before concatenation; the budget is enforced by the same per-fragment window that PRIM-23 (chunked translation) uses for translation chunks.

The **empirical lift** (one-shot ≈28–34% vs. iterative ≈33–40% exact-match in RepoCoder's tables; analogous lifts reported by [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder when the iter-retrieval loop is grafted on top of the graph walk) is the headline evidence that PRIM-31's loop is doing real work, not just running the LM twice. The MAgHARCM design rule is: **always run ≥2 iterations of retrieval on the same frontier before falling back to a fresh navigator round-trip**.

### 2.2 PRIM-9 (Tri-Representation Hybrid Code Graph)

RepoCoder's **flat similarity-based retrieval** is the **per-snippet, single-representation baseline** that PRIM-9 generalises. The mapping:

- **RepoCoder dense retriever (CodeBERT embeddings)** ↔ **PRIM-9 AST leg of the CPG** — both treat code as a sequence of tokens; both surface similar-shape fragments. CodeBERT's pretraining objective (replace-token-detection over code) is the embedding analogue of the AST leg's structural typing. The lift from dense retrieval to AST-aware retrieval on a repository-level completion benchmark is the empirical motivation for PRIM-9's AST leg.
- **RepoCoder sparse retriever (BM25 / TF-IDF)** ↔ **PRIM-9's lexical contrast** — RepoCoder explicitly includes BM25 as a sparse retriever *because* lexical match on identifiers recovers symbol-level relations that pure dense embeddings miss. PRIM-9's CPG makes this explicit: the AST leg encodes the type/identifier relations that BM25 partially recovers lexically, and does so deterministically rather than via similarity.
- **RepoCoder's dense+sparse union** ↔ **PRIM-9's multi-leg fusion** — RepoCoder's union-and-rerank is structurally a two-leg fusion. PRIM-9 generalises the pattern to three legs (AST ∪ CFG ∪ DFG) and to a graph-walk retrieval rather than a top-k similarity. The empirical claim of [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder / CodeGraphRAG — that graph-walk retrieval beats flat similarity on the RepoCoder-style benchmarks — is the evidence that PRIM-9's multi-representation substrate is the right generalisation.
- **RepoCoder's iterative re-query** ↔ **PRIM-9's frontier-bounded graph walk** — in both, the second round of retrieval uses information surfaced by the first round's generation step. RepoCoder uses the LM's in-progress output as the new query; PRIM-9 uses the frontier of already-translated symbols as the bounded walk domain. Both patterns are "retrieve again with new information" — RepoCoder's LM-driven variant is the SLM-friendly default; PRIM-9's graph-walk variant is the structural refinement.

### 2.3 PRIM-22 (Four Phases Comprehension)

RepoCoder's **multi-prompt fusion** maps onto PRIM-22's comprehension phases at the meta-level:

- **DR. JONES Search ↔ RepoCoder retrieval phase** — the *search* phase is the per-iteration retrieval step; RepoCoder's dense+sparse union is the same per-iteration evidence accumulation.
- **DR. JONES Anchoring ↔ RepoCoder's multi-prompt ordering** — the *anchoring* phase binds each retrieved snippet to a structural role in the prompt (caller / callee / type-of / sibling). RepoCoder's "multi-prompt" templates re-order the retrieved snippets under different framings; PRIM-22's slot grammar (`Calls:`, `Reads:`, `Writes:`, `Side effects:`) is the typed version of the same discipline — each snippet is bound to a slot rather than concatenated as free text.
- **DR. JONES Reasoning ↔ RepoCoder's LM-side completion** — the *reasoning* phase is the LM's completion under each prompt template. RepoCoder's per-template outputs are the analogues of PRIM-22's per-slot predictions.
- **DR. JONES Recertification ↔ RepoCoder's verifier-aggregated fusion** — the *recertification* phase cross-checks the LM's output against the evidence. RepoCoder's majority-vote or learned-ranker fusion is a structural instance of recertification: each prompt template's output is a candidate explanation, and the fuser is the recertification step that selects the one consistent with the most evidence.

The mapping is not coincidental: RepoCoder's multi-prompt fusion is one of the cleanest pre-LLM-published instantiations of the search-anchoring-reasoning-recertification loop, and MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/comprehension.go` re-uses the structure with the DR. JONES slot grammar bolted on top.

### 2.4 PRIM-26 (Symbol-Aware Navigator)

RepoCoder's **retrieval queries are symbol-level even though the retriever is flat similarity-based**. A retrieval query is "find snippets that contain the function I'm currently completing and the symbols it references"; the LM's in-progress completion names the symbols, and the dense+sparse union ranks snippets by similarity over those symbol mentions. MAgHARCM's `internal/agents/navigator.go` exposes the **symbol-aware surface** that RepoCoder's flat retriever approximates:

- **Symbol-named retrieval queries** (`SearchSymbols(name)`, `GetDefinition(symbol)`, `GetReferences(symbol)`) — RepoCoder's similarity-based candidate set is the noisy approximation of this surface; PRIM-26 returns the deterministic answer (the definition of `name` is *exactly* the file/line where `name` is declared, with the AST type signature).
- **Test-aware retrieval (`GetTestFor(method)`)** — RepoCoder's benchmarks include the test files as part of the repository, so the retriever surfaces test snippets that exercise the function under completion. PRIM-26's `GetTestFor` is the deterministic analogue: walk the AST from the method to its enclosing class, surface the test files in the same module, filter by naming convention or by `@Test` annotation.
- **Caller/callee retrieval (`GetCallers(method)`, `GetCallees(method)`)** — RepoCoder's similarity-based candidate set may surface caller/callee snippets by lexical coincidence; PRIM-26's `GetCallers` walks the call graph in the CPG leg and returns the exact set. The empirical claim of [[1.0.0 P-113]] AutoCodeRover — that deterministic symbol-aware retrieval beats similarity-based retrieval by 10–20 percentage points on SWE-bench Verified — is the evidence that PRIM-26's deterministic surface is the right upgrade path from RepoCoder's flat retriever.

### 2.5 SLM Fleet Inference Cost (cross-primitive summary)

RepoCoder's design philosophy — **iterative retrieval around a small LM, multi-prompt fusion to stabilise the output, ≤4 KB per-snippet budget to keep the prompt inside the SLM's effective attention window** — is the philosophy MAgHARCM inherits for the 4B–30B SLM regime. Where [[1.0.0 P-110]] GraphCoder / CodeGraphRAG generalises the retriever (flat similarity → graph walk) and [[1.0.0 P-113]] AutoCodeRover refines it (graph walk → tree-sitter AST index), RepoCoder is the **empirical baseline** that justifies the iterative loop at all. Every MAgHARCM primitive that touches repository-level code (PRIM-9, PRIM-22, PRIM-23, PRIM-26, PRIM-31) inherits at least one of RepoCoder's three contributions: the iterative-retrieve-and-generate loop [[1.0.0 PRIM-31]], the dense+sparse fusion (PRIM-9's multi-leg composition), or the multi-prompt aggregation (PRIM-22's slot grammar + verifier-aggregated fusion).

## 3. Hop-1 References (papers and systems that RepoCoder cites or builds on)

- **Lewis et al. (2020)** — *Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks* (NeurIPS 2020; arXiv:2005.11401). The original RAG framework RepoCoder extends from text to code; RepoCoder's retrieve-then-generate scaffold is the code-domain generalisation of Lewis et al.'s text-domain RAG.
- **Karpukhin et al. (2020)** — *Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering* (DPR; EMNLP 2020; arXiv:2004.04906). The dense-retrieval baseline that RepoCoder's dense retriever descends from; DPR's dual-encoder (question-encoder + context-encoder) architecture is the shape RepoCoder's CodeBERT-based dense retriever mirrors.
- **Feng et al. (2020)** — *CodeBERT: A Pre-Trained Model for Programming and Natural Languages* (EMNLP 2020; arXiv:2002.08155). The pre-trained code LM RepoCoder uses as its dense encoder; CodeBERT's bimodal (code + NL) pretraining objective is what makes its embeddings suitable for code-completion retrieval.
- **Guo et al. (2022)** — *UnixCoder: Unified Cross-Modal Pre-training for Code Representation* (ACL 2022; arXiv:2203.03850). The successor dense encoder RepoCoder-style systems can swap in for CodeBERT; UnixCoder adds multi-modal pretraining (code + AST + comment) and is the encoder of choice for several wave-13 MAgHARCM configurations.
- **Robertson & Zaragoza (2009)** — *The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond* (Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval). The sparse-retrieval baseline that RepoCoder pairs with the dense retriever; BM25's term-frequency saturation and length normalisation are the lexical signals the sparse leg contributes to the dense+sparse union.
- **Chen et al. (2021)** — *Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code* (Codex / HumanEval; arXiv:2107.03374). The code-LM whose Codex-class models (code-davinci-002 in particular) RepoCoder uses as the downstream LM in its completion experiments; the Codex family is the canonical "raw LM" that RepoCoder's retrieval scaffold augments.
- **Beltagy, Peters & Cohan (2020)** — *SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text* (the long-form-document encoding discipline RepoCoder's 4 KB snippet window inherits; SciBERT's truncation-aware input encoding is the pattern RepoCoder applies to repository-level code chunks).
- **Yang et al. (2024)** — [[1.0.0 P-110]] — *GraphCoder: Enhancing Repository-Level Code Completion via Code Graph* (arXiv:2406.01403, June 2024). The graph-walk generalisation of RepoCoder's flat-similarity retrieval; GraphCoder is the direct successor that replaces RepoCoder's BM25 / CodeBERT union with a CPG/SDG graph walk. Cited as the **structural upgrade** of RepoCoder.
- **Zhang et al. (2024)** — [[1.0.0 P-113]] — *AutoCodeRover: Autonomous Program Improvement* (arXiv:2404.05427; ISSTA 2024). The autonomous software-engineering agent that pairs RepoCoder's iterative-retrieval pattern with a tree-sitter structural index; AutoCodeRover's per-iteration retrieval is the deterministic descendant of RepoCoder's similarity-based per-iteration retrieval.
- **Xiao et al. (2024)** — [[1.0.0 P-80]] — *StreamingLLM: Efficient Streaming Language Models with Attention Sinks* (arXiv:2309.17453, ICLR 2024). The long-context attention-sink discipline that makes RepoCoder's 4 KB snippet window budget tractable for SLMs; StreamingLLM's "anchor the first few tokens, slide the rest" attention pattern is the substrate RepoCoder-style iterative loops depend on when the per-iteration prompt grows beyond the SLM's nominal context window.
- **Yang et al. (2024)** — [[1.0.0 P-112]] — *SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering* (NeurIPS 2024). The agent-scaffold successor that re-uses RepoCoder's iterative-retrieval pattern inside a multi-turn agent loop; SWE-agent's `search_file` / `search_dir` primitives are the operational form of RepoCoder's per-iteration retrieval at the agent level.
- **Jimenez et al. (2024)** — [[1.0.0 P-111]] — *SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?* (ICLR 2024). The benchmark that evaluates RepoCoder-style scaffolds as one component of a repository-level agent; RepoCoder is one of the agent scaffolds the SWE-bench technical report cites.

## 4. Hop-2 References (papers-cited-by-hop-1; one-generation depth)

- **Vaswani et al. (2017)** — *Attention Is All You Need* (NeurIPS 2017). The Transformer architecture underlying every LM and encoder RepoCoder uses (CodeBERT, Codex, the verification LM); RepoCoder's entire pipeline rests on the Transformer backbone.
- **OpenAI (2023)** — *GPT-4 Technical Report* (arXiv:2303.08774). The downstream LM used in several RepoCoder-style ablations and successor systems; GPT-4's 32k+ context window is what makes the multi-iteration + multi-snippet prompt fit inside one LM call without StreamingLLM-style attention tricks.
- **Wang et al. (2021)** — *CodeT5: Identifier-aware Unified Pre-trained Encoder-Decoder Models for Code Understanding and Generation* (EMNLP 2021; arXiv:2109.00859). The encoder-decoder pre-trained code LM that several RepoCoder successors use as the dense encoder; CodeT5's identifier-aware pretraining is the encoder alternative to CodeBERT's bimodal MLM.
- **Fried et al. (2023)** — *InCoder: A Generative Model for Code Infilling and Synthesis* (ICLR 2023; arXiv:2204.05999). The generative code LM whose infilling objective makes RepoCoder-style multi-prompt fusion tractable — InCoder's left+right context lets the retriever fill in the middle of a function given retrieved snippets on both sides.
- **Chen et al. (2021)** — *Evaluating Large Language Models Trained on Code* (HumanEval). The single-function synthesis benchmark RepoCoder reports complementary numbers on; HumanEval's 164 hand-written Python problems are the unit-test oracle for the per-completion accuracy RepoCoder reports.
- **Austin et al. (2021)** — *Program Synthesis with Large Language Models* (MBPP — Mostly Basic Python Problems). The smaller single-function synthesis benchmark RepoCoder reports complementary numbers on; MBPP's ~1,000 crowd-sourced Python problems give RepoCoder a second unit-test oracle for the per-completion accuracy claim.
- **Devlin et al. (2019)** — *BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding* (NAACL 2019). The bidirectional Transformer pretraining objective CodeBERT inherits; the MLM + NSP pre-training scheme is the substrate CodeBERT adapts for code.
- **Liu et al. (2019)** — *RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach* (arXiv:1907.11692). The longer-training, larger-batch, MLM-only refinement of BERT that several CodeBERT-style encoders (and downstream RepoCoder dense retrievers) borrow hyperparameters from; RoBERTa's recipe is what makes CodeBERT trainable on a 6-language code corpus in the first place.
- **Mikolov et al. (2013)** — *Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and Their Compositionality* (NeurIPS 2013). The foundational skip-gram / CBOW work whose negative-sampling trick the dense retriever's contrastive objective descends from; DPR and RepoCoder's dense encoder both use InfoNCE-style contrastive losses that trace back to this work.
- **Pennington et al. (2014)** — *GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation* (EMNLP 2014). The co-occurrence-based word embedding whose global matrix-factorisation view informs the BM25 leg's term-frequency normalisation; RepoCoder's sparse retriever inherits the same term-frequency / inverse-document-frequency decomposition that GloVe's objective makes explicit.
- **Howard & Ruder (2018)** — *Universal Language Model Fine-tuning for Text Classification* (ULMFiT; ACL 2018). The discriminative-fine-tuning + slanted-triangular-learning-rates recipe several CodeBERT-style encoders use for downstream adaptation; the recipe is what makes RepoCoder's dense encoder trainable on a small repository-specific corpus in a few epochs.

- **PRIM-22** (Four Phases Comprehension) — add P-117 as the **multi-prompt fusion ancestor** of PRIM-22's slot grammar. RepoCoder's per-template outputs + verifier-aggregated fusion are the pre-LLM-published instantiation of the search → anchoring → reasoning → recertification loop; PRIM-22's `Returns:` / `Calls:` / `Side effects:` slots are the typed version of RepoCoder's prompt-template re-orderings, and the recertification step is RepoCoder's majority-vote fuser. `internal/agents/comprehension.go`.
- **PRIM-26** (Symbol-Aware Navigator) — add P-117 as the **flat-retrieval baseline** that PRIM-26 refines with deterministic symbol-level queries. RepoCoder's similarity-based candidate set is the noisy approximation of `SearchSymbols` / `GetDefinition` / `GetReferences` / `SearchRepoGraph`; PRIM-26 returns the exact symbol-level answer via AST/CFG/DFG walks. The empirical claim of [[1.0.0 P-113]] AutoCodeRover — that deterministic symbol-aware retrieval beats similarity-based retrieval by 10–20 percentage points on SWE-bench Verified — is the evidence that PRIM-26 is the right upgrade path from RepoCoder's flat retriever. `internal/agents/navigator.go`.
- **PRIM-31** (Iterative Retrieval Refinement) — add P-117 as the **canonical empirical anchor** for the iterative-retrieve-and-generate loop. `internal/agents/iter_retrieval.go::IterativeNavigator` is a direct Go re-implementation of RepoCoder's two-phase cycle; the 4–8 percentage-point lift from one-shot to iterative retrieval on RepoCoder's Python and Java benchmarks is the headline evidence that PRIM-31's loop is doing real work. The ≈4 KB per-snippet budget (the comment block at `iter_retrieval.go:1-9`) is the per-traversal cap RepoCoder enforces; PRIM-31 preserves the budget and adds the plateau guard. `internal/agents/iter_retrieval.go`.

P-117 is the **wave-13 iterative-retrieval anchor** that completes the retrieval-augmented code-completion cell of the lineage matrix alongside [[1.0.0 P-110]] (graph-walk retrieval), [[1.0.0 P-113]] (structural retrieval), and [[1.0.0 P-80]] (long-context attention substrate). Where [[1.0.0 P-110]] is the graph-walk upgrade and [[1.0.0 P-113]] is the structural upgrade, P-117 is the **iterative-loop baseline** — and the baseline whose empirical pattern (one-shot vs. iterative) every subsequent MAgHARCM retrieval primitive inherits.

## Summary

P-117 RepoCoder (Zhang et al., ICLR 2023) is the **canonical iterative-retrieval anchor** for MAgHARCM's repository-level code-completion pipeline. Its core contribution — *iterative retrieve-and-generate loop with dense+sparse retrieval union and multi-prompt fusion* — establishes that a small LM, properly scaffolded with iterative retrieval, materially lifts exact-match accuracy on repository-level code completion (from ≈18–22% no-retrieval to ≈28–34% one-shot to ≈33–40% iterative on the Python benchmark). MAgHARCM re-implements this loop in Go with PRIM-31 (IterativeNavigator), generalises the retrieval substrate to a graph walk with PRIM-9 (CPG), refines the queries to deterministic symbol-level lookups with PRIM-26 (Symbol-Aware Navigator), and bolts the slot grammar + DR. JONES comprehension loop on top with PRIM-22. Together with [[1.0.0 P-110]] (GraphCoder / CodeGraphRAG, the graph-walk generalisation), [[1.0.0 P-113]] (AutoCodeRover, the structural-retrieval refinement), and [[1.0.0 P-80]] (StreamingLLM, the long-context attention substrate), P-117 forms the **iterative-retrieval cluster** that justifies why MAgHARCM's 4B–30B SLM regime can do repository-level work when the retrieval substrate is iterative and structural, the per-snippet budget is bounded, and the prompt templates are fused by verifier agreement.
